content: Cefotetan disodium is a second-generation cephalosporin antibiotic approved by the FDA for the treatment of various bacterial infections, including urinary tract infections, lower respiratory tract infections, skin and skin structure infections, gynecologic infections, intra-abdominal infections, and bone and joint infections. It is also used for the prevention of postoperative infections in certain surgical procedures. The drug is administered intravenously, with dosages varying based on the type and severity of the infection. Indications and Dosage for Adults: 1. Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): Caused by Escherichia coli, Klebsiella spp., Proteus mirabilis, and other Proteus species. Dosage: 500 mg every 12 hours IV, or 1–2 g every 24 hours IV, or 1–2 g every 12 hours IV. 2. Lower Respiratory Tract Infections: Caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus (both penicillinase-producing and non-penicillinase-producing strains), Haemophilus influenzae (including ampicillin-resistant strains), Klebsiella spp., E. coli, Proteus mirabilis, and Serratia marcescens. Dosage: 1–2 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. Severe cases: 2 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. Life-threatening cases: 3 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. 3. Skin and Skin Structure Infections: Caused by Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus epidermidis, Streptococcus pyogenes, E. coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and anaerobic organisms like Peptococcus niger and Peptostreptococcus spp. Mild to moderate cases: 2 g every 24 hours IV or 1 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. Severe cases: 2 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. 4. Gynecologic Infections: Caused by Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus epidermidis, Streptococcus spp., E. coli, Proteus mirabilis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Bacteroides spp., and Fusobacterium spp. Dosage: 1–2 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. Severe cases: 2 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. Life-threatening cases: 3 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. Note: Cefotetan does not cover Chlamydia trachomatis. If this pathogen is suspected, additional antichlamydial therapy is required. 5. Intra-abdominal Infections: Caused by E. coli, Klebsiella spp., Streptococcus spp., Bacteroides spp., and Clostridium spp. Dosage: 1–2 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. Severe cases: 2 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. Life-threatening cases: 3 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. 6. Bone and Joint Infections: Caused by Staphylococcus aureus. Dosage: 1–2 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. Severe cases: 2 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. Life-threatening cases: 3 g every 12 hours IV for 5–10 days. 7. Surgical Prophylaxis: Administered preoperatively to reduce the risk of postoperative infections in clean-contaminated or potentially contaminated surgeries (e.g. Dosage: 1–2 g IV once, 30–60 minutes before surgery. Pediatric Use: The safety and efficacy of cefotetan in pediatric patients have not been established. Contraindications: Patients with known hypersensitivity to cephalosporins. Patients with a history of cephalosporin-associated hemolytic anemia. Warnings: 1. Hypersensitivity Reactions: Patients with a history of penicillin allergy may have cross-reactivity with cefotetan. Severe hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, may occur. If an allergic reaction develops, discontinue the drug immediately and provide emergency treatment as needed (e.g., epinephrine, corticosteroids, antihistamines, airway management). 2. Hemolytic Anemia: Immune-mediated hemolytic anemia has been reported with cefotetan use, including rare fatal cases. Patients should be monitored for signs of anemia, and the drug should be discontinued if hemolytic anemia is suspected. Blood transfusions may be required in severe cases. 3. Clostridium difficile-Associated Diarrhea (CDAD): Antibiotic use can disrupt normal gut flora, leading to overgrowth of C. difficile. Symptoms range from mild diarrhea to life-threatening colitis. If CDAD is suspected, discontinue unnecessary antibiotics and initiate appropriate treatment. 4. Prothrombin Activity: Cefotetan may cause a reduction in prothrombin activity, increasing the risk of bleeding. Patients at higher risk include those with renal or hepatic impairment, malnutrition, cancer, or advanced age. Prothrombin time should be monitored, and vitamin K supplementation may be required. Adverse Reactions: 1. Gastrointestinal: Diarrhea, nausea, pseudomembranous colitis. 2. Hematologic: Eosinophilia, thrombocytosis, positive Coombs test, hemolytic anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, prolonged prothrombin time. 3. Hepatic: Elevated liver enzymes (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, LDH). 4. Hypersensitivity: Rash, itching, anaphylaxis, urticaria. 5. Local Reactions: Phlebitis and discomfort at the injection site. 6. Renal: Rare cases of nephrotoxicity. 7. Miscellaneous: Fever, superinfection, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis. Drug Interactions: Concomitant use with aminoglycosides may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity. Renal function should be closely monitored. Cefotetan may cause false-positive results in urine glucose tests using non-enzymatic methods (e.g., Clinitest®, Benedict’s solution). Enzymatic glucose oxidase tests are recommended. Use in Specific Populations: 1. Pregnancy: Classified as Category B. Animal studies have shown no harm to the fetus, but adequate human studies are lacking. Use only if clearly needed. 2. Nursing Mothers: Excreted in low concentrations in breast milk. Use with caution. 3. Geriatric Patients: No significant differences in safety or efficacy compared to younger patients, but renal function should be monitored due to the risk of drug accumulation. 4. Renal Impairment: Dosage adjustments are necessary based on creatinine clearance. 5. Pediatric Patients: Safety and efficacy not established. Pharmacokinetics: Cefotetan is 88% plasma protein-bound and has a half-life of 3–4.6 hours. It is primarily excreted unchanged in the urine, with 51–81% of the dose recovered within 24 hours. Therapeutic concentrations are achieved in various tissues and fluids, including skin, muscle, bile, bladder, and peritoneal fluid. Storage: Store at 20° to 25°C (68° to 77°F). Patient Counseling: Patients should be informed about the potential for diarrhea, including severe cases of watery or bloody stools, even weeks after completing therapy. They should complete the full course of treatment as prescribed to prevent bacterial resistance. Alcohol consumption should be avoided for 72 hours after cefotetan administration due to the risk of a disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, sweating, headache, tachycardia).
